assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly consequential framework for understanding persistent cross-country income gaps through the allocation of resources across firms.
assessment.attribution: The three proposed laureates provide a coherent theoretical and quantitative account of misallocation and its aggregate consequences.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has been extensively used in growth, development and firm-dynamics research and is mature enough for recognition.
uncertainties: The quantitative size and precise sources of misallocation remain sensitive to measurement and modeling choices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis of collateral constraints and financial amplification transformed macroeconomic accounts of credit cycles and crises.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore supplied a central collateral mechanism, while Gertler made foundational contributions to the financial-accelerator framework.
assessment.maturity: The mechanisms have endured through multiple business-cycle and financial-crisis applications.
uncertainties: The broad candidate grouping spans related but distinguishable models, making any three-person attribution necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work fundamentally changed empirical understanding of how technology, trade and tasks reshape labor demand and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson form a well-defined core for the task and trade-shock evidence; their proposed credit is readily intelligible.
assessment.maturity: Its findings have prompted a large literature and remain central to debates over globalization and technological change.
uncertainties: Causal magnitudes and the relative roles of trade, technology and local adjustment remain contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection supplied a powerful and durable reorientation of modern trade theory and quantitative trade analysis.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is central to the canonical framework, with Helpman and Redding making major complementary contributions to its development and applications.
assessment.maturity: The approach is deeply integrated into theoretical and empirical international-trade research.
uncertainties: The relevant intellectual lineage is broad, so delimiting recognition to three contributors is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models materially improved the analysis of distributional channels in macroeconomic policy.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll and Violante provide a clear core group for the modern quantitative framework.
assessment.maturity: The approach has rapidly become influential in policy analysis and macroeconomic research.
uncertainties: Its relatively recent development leaves less time to assess which modeling ingredients will prove permanently fundamental.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Political-economy research on institutions, electoral incentives, state capacity and fiscal policy has reshaped analysis of policy formation.
assessment.attribution: Persson, Tabellini and Besley represent a coherent set of leading foundational contributions.
assessment.maturity: The theories have generated a long-lived empirical and institutional research program.
uncertainties: The field encompasses several distinct contributions, which complicates a single prize citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The study of reciprocity, fairness and inequity aversion substantially altered economic models of behavior and institutions.
assessment.attribution: Fehr, Falk and Schmidt made complementary experimental and theoretical contributions to a recognizable body of work.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have been repeatedly tested and incorporated across behavioral, labor and organizational economics.
uncertainties: The scope and stability of social-preference parameters across settings remain an active empirical question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evolutionary analysis of routines and organizational change offered a durable alternative perspective on firm behavior, innovation and economic dynamism.
assessment.attribution: Winter is an indispensable contributor to this intellectual tradition and is appropriately identified in the candidate entry.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has had longstanding influence across organizational and evolutionary economics.
uncertainties: The listed attribution may not fully represent the wider collaborative intellectual lineage of evolutionary economics.
Its aggregate empirical implications are less unified than those of some higher-ranked candidates.
